jobs.title: (Junior) Data Engineer | Knowledge Graphs & Pharma Data (f/m/d)
jobs.description: Become a Part of Accurids Join us and help make medicinal product data useful for all! At Accurids, we build the data backbone behind life-science innovation. Our platform identifies, links and standardizes critical enterprise data in line with global standards such as the ISO standard for the Identification of Medicinal Products (IDMP), and some of the world's largest pharma companies use it to bring products to patients faster and more safely. You will join our Services department, a group of interdisciplinary experts who help our pharma customers adopt our platform and make it truly useful for their data. Within it, you are part of the data engineering team, which works in a clear, well-documented way: state-of-the-art tools, flexible processes, and agentic AI used in a structured, reliable way. You see your results in live customer projects within weeks, and learn the pharma data domain from people who have worked in it for years. How you’ll make an impact: You transform data from a wide range of structured sources (such as CSV, JSON, RDF, and SQL and NoSQL databases) into the IDMP data model, and build the pipelines that keep it up to date. You use AI to turn unstructured sources such as documents and texts into structured, verifiable data. You bring a DevOps mindset to data: with AI as your everyday tool, used responsibly, you keep data flows and tooling tested, automated, documented and reliable, as the regulated pharma industry demands. You support the design of data models for IDMP knowledge graphs, leveraging the IDMP ontology, and learn to navigate graphs with SPARQL and agentic tooling. As part of a joint team with our customers, you work directly with their domain experts to understand their data and make their medicinal product data useful. What helps you succeed: A background in computer science, data science or a life-science subject such as biology, chemistry or pharmacy. A formal degree is welcome but not required. First hands-on experience in data

jobs.title: Location Data engineer
jobs.description: We are seeking a highly skilled Location Data Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will work with large-scale datasets generated by our products and turn raw data into meaningful signals, insights, and features. You will work across the entire data lifecycle: building reliable pipelines, exploring and understanding complex datasets, developing features from them, and creating the tools and visualizations needed to understand their quality and impact. This is a technical and product-oriented data role. You'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, and data teams to find what we can learn from our data and turn those learnings into production systems. As a Data Engineer, your day-to-day will include: Making Sense of Data Explore large and complex datasets to understand user behavior and identify useful patterns and signals. Transform raw data into reliable, well-defined features that can be used by our products and engineering teams. Develop a deep understanding of our data: where it comes from, what it represents, its limitations, and how it can be combined to answer new questions. Building Data Products Design, build, and maintain pipelines that process large volumes of data efficiently and reliably. Take ideas from exploration to production: prototype them on historical data, evaluate their quality, and build the pipelines needed to run them at scale. Build datasets and features that can power product experiences, internal systems, analytics, and machine learning models. Work with technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or similar tools depending on the problem at hand. Exploring & Analyzing Use data to investigate hypotheses, understand behaviors, and answer ambiguous questions. Develop metrics and evaluation frameworks to understand whether the signals and features we build actually work. Create analyses, dashboards, and visualizations that make complex datasets understandable and help the team make better decisions
